ground_truth_diagnosis: RecommendationService pods are OOMKilled (exit 137) because -Xmx1024m lets the JVM heap alone use the entire 1Gi container limit. Metaspace, thread stacks and GC structures have no room, so the kernel sends SIGKILL before the JVM can throw an OutOfMemoryError.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: RecommendationService's OOMKilled code is registered as Container Memory (SEV-3, Recommendations-Team) with a 1024 MiB memory limit and a 1024 MB JVM max heap.
A heap sized to the full container limit leaves no room for non-heap JVM memory, so the kernel kills the container before any Java error is logged.

ground_truth_remediation: Replace -Xmx1024m with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 in the deployment manifest

user_input: Our recommendation pods restart more often during peak hours, roughly every few hours, and the app logs show nothing before each restart. Memory climbs steadily as more users browse. What's causing this and how do we stop it?
ground_truth_diagnosis: RecommendationService is restarting with OOMKilled because its user embedding cache has no size limit or eviction. Memory grows with the number of active users until it reaches the 1Gi container limit. Restarts tracking high-traffic periods point to the cache as the main cause.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: The OOMKilled code for RecommendationService is registered with a 1024 MiB memory limit.
The user embedding cache has no size limit or eviction, so memory grows with active users until the container is killed.

ground_truth_remediation: Limit the embedding cache size and add LRU eviction (for example 200,000 entries)

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: The CrashLoopBackOff code for InventoryService is registered with a liveness failure threshold of 3.

user_input: Our checkout pods on worker-node-3 keep getting Evicted even though their own usage looks fine, and nothing in our service changed. Which workload is filling the node's disk, and why do unrelated pods get killed?
ground_truth_diagnosis: ImageService is filling the node's ephemeral storage with temporary files from failed resizes. Because ImageService has no ephemeral-storage limits, one pod can consume the whole node disk, so the kubelet evicts pods across the node, including unrelated checkout pods.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: The Evicted code for ImageService is registered as Node Resource Pressure with a 10% nodefs eviction threshold.
Without ephemeral-storage limits, one pod can consume the whole node disk, so the kubelet evicts pods across the node instead of only the offending pod.

ground_truth_remediation: Set ephemeral-storage requests and limits on image-service (request 2Gi, limit 4Gi)
Delete temporary files in a finally block so failed resizes do not leak them

user_input: Why do recommendation pods keep dying with exit code 137 and no error in the app logs? They restart every few hours, and the previous container's logs just stop. Is this a memory problem?
ground_truth_diagnosis: RecommendationService is OOMKilled because its JVM heap is set to -Xmx1024m, which equals the full 1Gi container limit. Heap plus non-heap memory exceeds the limit, so the kernel sends SIGKILL, and no Java error is logged.

expected_evidence_mapping.claim: The OOMKilled code for RecommendationService is registered with a 1024 MiB memory limit and a 1024 MB JVM max heap.
A heap sized to the full container limit leaves no room for non-heap JVM memory, so SIGKILL arrives before any Java error is logged.

ground_truth_remediation: Replace -Xmx1024m with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 in the deployment manifest
